title: Causality Guided Representation Learning for Cross-Style Hate Speech Detection
measurement_description: The paper evaluated models on their ability to perform cross-style (explicit vs. implicit) hate speech detection. While religion was not the primary focus, it was included as one of the demographic target groups for hate speech within the evaluated datasets (alongside gender, race, social class, and disability) to test if the model could disentangle hateful intent from superficial stylistic linguistic cues.
findings: The paper did not report findings specific to religion. Overall, it found that standard LLMs and traditional baseline models frequently over-predict hate when trained on explicit datasets, or under-predict when tested on implicit variants. The proposed causal representation learning framework, CADET, successfully disentangled hate intent from stylistic cues, leading to robust cross-style hate speech detection across all target demographics (which includes religion as a target variable).
references: Kartik Ahuja, Divyat Mahajan, Yixin Wang, and Yoshua Bengio. 2023. Interventional causal representation learning. In International conference on machine learning. PMLR, 372–407.
